This wall of text talks about having a guided structure for a better debate culture: I assume that a better environment leads to better behavior.

Mods: there is a very large list of reasons why we need em. Another way of looking at it, is we invoke an authority to compensate for "the flaws in the system" or lets find somebody willing to sacrifice him/her self to play whack-a-mole. Lets also not forget about the secondary conflicts about whether or not the mods abuse their power. The whack-a-mole strategy scales badly: just look at reddit.

new debate friendly thread style:

IMHO: the biggest "flaw in the system" is "we" let people debate each other without FIRST agreeing on a common set of base-assumptions about the world that are relevant to the subject of debate. This shows especially in the comment-wars about religion and politics.

base-assumptions can be:

a) necessary guesses about the world that however can neither be proven nor disproved by facts
b) scientific facts

I propose to introduce a 3-stage debate-style:

1 list base assumptions
2 make logical arguments that assume the base assumptions to be true
3 draw conclusions from arguments

open-source-debate: So what if i don't agree with the base assumptions ? Fork the debate, basically make a copy and modify the base assumption.

This way the mods need to spend less energy on ending derailed debates, and we can reduce the waste of effort that comes from people fighting pointless ideological wars that arise from incompatible outlooks on the world.

Yes I'm proposing segregation, because I don't see people changing their base assumptions. I think many base-assumptions about the world arise from biological traits like risk tolerance, . Nobody changes their biology. (there is circumstantial evidence that a larger amygdala in your brain makes you more conservative) Note this might be sudo scientific nonsense

In the end people have to choose which base assumptions they accept or reject. This makes it more transparent and easier to do, and probably allot more peaceful.

the specifics:

the opening post contains 3 boxes (assumptions, arguments and conclusions)
every subsequent post only contains 2 boxes (arguments and conclusions)

every subsequent poster has to click "agree-to-post" below the box of assumptions,

if s/he clicks "disagree-to-fork" :

if no forks exist -> create fork & let poster modify list of assumptions
if other forks already exist -> let user choose between joining an existing fork or creating a new one.

I suggest contextual tags for list of assumptions:

"alternate reality" -tag for base assumptions that defy actual facts

the alternate reality -tag can only be self imposed remember: avoid whack-a-mole strategy
this basically just says we're having fun we like to pretend, so contain the vitriol

"reality checked" -tag that needs citations of sources(1) that proves the factual accuracy

this basically signals: we're dead serious we do our research & know our stuff.
this tag can be earned by approval of your peers that in turn stake their distinguished status by approving.
this tag is available to distinguished posters those that have a history of approving or writing factual posts
this tag can be removed by mods in case somebody is citing illegitimate sources.

(1) sources can also be another subverse that justifies a base assumption.

...

I consider this a draft proposal,

thanks for reading
reducing mod workload, enabling more constructive debate, having less ideological turf-wars.

My apologies for the the lack of clarity, I tend to conceptualize my ideas visually & it is very hard to translate that in to a compelling text.

Anyway my point was, that humans can be nice & productive, given the right environment. I am convinced that the need for mods can be greatly reduced if the structure of the website compels more people to contribute, instead of bickering.

I tend to look at people as a constant that can't be changed, & the environment as the variable. If you rely on mods to force people to "behave", you are essentially forcing people to invest willpower to adapt to the environment. Willpower is a very scarce resource. When people run out of willpower, you get to see the undesirable side of humanity. I think that we need to be mindful to conserve the willpower of others. I realize that it is very hard to summon the necessary empathy, to realize that allot of the nasty behavior is born out of frustration, & not ill will.

The goal of my proposal is to segregate people that hold world-views that are irreconcilable, as well as making it easier to have a dialog rather then a shouting match. I think that agreeing on base assumption before engaging in a debate is vital. I think that the structure of the website should aim to naturally induce beneficial behavior.

IMHO: Reddit very often relies on rather authoritarian moderation, this often leads to resentment and disruptive behavior.

I have the suspicion that astroturfing is on the rise, if moderators are preoccupied with "babysitting", they will not be able to defend us against such deceitful actions.

I think that most of reddit is an example of corrupt moderation, the mods stick to their own agenda and only enforce the rules when they are very blatantly broken or when it is convenient to enforce. Some other subs are waaaaaaay to lenient. Polandball is authoritarian, but it is very effective at keeping a good environment. And change is fairly easy with the right environment - an environment that I feel that Polandball has achieved.

When I say environment, I mean the design & functionality of the website, not the people that "inhabit" it. So in this very specific context you cannot "keep a good environment", you can only build/design a good environment.

Corruption mostly is a matter of degree. Take me for an example: Everything that i say & do is informed by my world-view, and my world-view is heavily influenced by my interests. Hence I too am guilty of furthering my agenda.

I do not think that it is possible to have an objective point of view free of all selfish biases, which pretty much makes it impossible to have a truly fair moderator. The same is true for the measuring of corruption. If i measure the degree of corruption of an authority, my verdict is going to be more damning the wider the gap between the respective world-views.

Moderators are a bit like judges. Even highly trained individuals regularly reach very different conclusions about right and wrong.

When ever one invokes authorities, they will use their power to further their agenda, even the most ethical individual will do this. It is not a matter bad intentions, it is the natural conclusion of a hierarchy.

"Keeping the peace" can be achieved by authoritative moderating, but you always have to be aware that you are paying a price for that. As it stands now Freedom always entails a certain degree of chaos.

I believe that the ultimate purpose of the Internet is to reduce authoritative "coercion" and build new democratic technologies that enable us to find the best possible compromise. I happen to think that this entails to separate people by the degree of how incompatible their world-views are.
The moderators of /r/polandball do not appear to be furthering their agenda, they are there furthering the agenda of /r/polandball - to aggregate non-shitty polandball comics.

I suggest you look at a thread about feminism, atheism or Islam, and then you can see how relentless people can talk past each other. It's just like tribal feuds.

I think polandball comics are pretty diverse, and the users are from all over he world. They touch on a lot of sensitive things too, like the holocaust or stuff like that, and yet the comment sections are very civil and such.
